classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the return direction from the island, choose an acute angle and inverse tangent ratio, then convert the northwest direction to a clockwise true bearing.

content.prompt:
A plane departed Sydney and flew due south for 350 km.
It then turned and flew due east for 500 km before landing on an island.
Calculate the bearing from the island to Sydney to the nearest degree.

spec.description: Sydney lies above an unnamed right-angle vertex; the island lies east of that vertex. Both named endpoints have N/E/S/W compass cues. Ordinary source colours are replaced by black.
spec.mathematics: The south and east legs have ratio 350:500. The requested direction is from the island northwest to Sydney. The supplied figure has no distance labels or bearing arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated angle or bearing is shown.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the acute angle west of north at the island.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta &= \frac{500}{350}\\\theta &= \tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{500}{350}\right)\\\text{Bearing} &= 360^{\circ}-\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{500}{350}\right)\\&\approx 305^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The bearing from the island to Sydney is $305^{\circ}$, to the nearest degree.
